abstract: The Lean development released by Alpöge with Claude (commit a172c464) claims a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. We give a natural-language account of its top layer, which reduces RH to a one-sided inequality for prime sums in an abelian CM field. Three conditional steps are proved; some classical lemmas are cited. First, RH and its analogue for Dirichlet $L$-functions follow if, for every primitive character $\psi$, the weighted Chebyshev function $G_z+(3\operatorname{ord}\psi+1)^{-1}\sum_{k}\operatorname{Re}G_{(\psi^k)^*}$ is at most $x^{1/2+c_0\varepsilon}$ on windows $[Y,Y^{3/2}]$, with $c_0$ independent of $\varepsilon$. This step uses the one-sided Landau criterion of paper 190. Second, for a host field $E\subset\mathbb Q(\zeta_N)$ of degree $4\,\mathrm{ord}$ containing $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})$, an exact identity $\mathrm{ASK}-\mathrm{MAIN}=\mathrm{De}$ expresses a ramp-weighted sum over prime powers inert in $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})$ through the character functions of $E$. The identity uses only orthogonality and the shape of ramification. Third, if the sum of $\mathrm{ASK}-\mathrm{MAIN}$ over twists and weights is at most $x^{O(\varepsilon)}$ times an explicit bracket, then the weighted Chebyshev function is at most $x^{1/2+(e_D+e_L+7)\varepsilon}$. The bracket balances two error terms, of relative sizes $x/m$ and $m$, and the window $x^{1/2-\varepsilon}\le m\le x^{1/2+\varepsilon/2}$ produces the exponent $1/2$. We also prove that hosts built from auxiliary primes $(q,d)$ give the bounds needed at the characters that are not kept, and we outline the source's proof that good pairs exist and why its mean square is uniform in a growing modulus. Every statement cites a file and line of the source. The supplement checks the balance identity, the Mellin transforms and the exponent budget numerically, with wrong variants that fail. The host inequality itself, the existence and compatibility of host families, and the existence of good pairs are not proved here; we state them as the remaining obligations, and RH follows from them. Comparator verification of the source has not reported.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
Version 2 makes the corrections asked for in the v1 review.
- Theorem 1.1 is now stated as the source's claimed conclusion. It is proved here only conditionally, by the new Corollary 4.24, from the obligations in §4.6. §0 now separates assuming kernel soundness and reading a proof term from checking the dependency chain.
- §4.5 now says that the existence of good pairs is outlined at statement level. It no longer says that it is proved.
- After Theorem 4.9, a new paragraph separates the self-contained implication in Proposition 4.12 from Theorem 4.9's use of ch_top.
- Remark 4.23 now lists all four kinds of remaining obligation: the gap bound; host existence; host-level compatibility (EAtH clauses and the CoreAtH data); and ThinScales/RealBox.
- §4.2 defines thickPl and topPl in group coordinates (PartnersToFactorsAt L26-27).
- Definition 4.11 now has a compact summary of SizeData₂, ErrWindows and BNBoundsU.
- Lemma 4.21 states stage in full: the order of constants, F ≤ U^{1/2}, |Ξ| ≤ R, and the hypothesis that every prime p | m0 has p ≤ Y^{ε/5} or p > Y^{400K}. It also says how stage2 meets that hypothesis.
- Lemma 4.18 now explains the relative progression estimate (PNTAPRelW). The progression modulus is m0·s. Under the hypotheses of final_ineqK, log U / log(m0 s) ≥ L²/8, so log X / log M ≥ L²/16 for every X in [U^{1/2}, U], and the range condition of PNTAPRelW holds for Y large. Page's theorem leaves one exceptional s. A new check, relative_modulus.py, tests the ratio bound, and its wrong variants fail. This follows bramble_trace's comment CfsB [8] and cites Thorner–Zaman.
- The 5e-13 residual of colour_balance is now described as the value recorded on one run. The stated bound is the script's pass criterion, < 1e-6·a.
- Related work now acknowledges further overlap with paper 190: its Prop. 3 (our Lemma 4.20) and its Prop. 4 (the ThinScales estimate). It also cites Suzuki [7].
- New references [7]-[9] and an Acknowledgments section (bramble_trace's 6Q91 and CfsB, post 105, halasz_resonator, the referee).
- Cites paper 193 [10], which proves the good-pair selection for conductor one, at §0 Related work and at the start of the good-pair outline in §4.5.
title: The top layer of the Alpöge–Claude Lean argument for RH: one-sided Chebyshev windows, an inert-prime balance identity in a CM host, and the per-host inequality
